notes: Savage Wind Configuration: the start screen's SETTINGS window shows tabs Prelaunch, Controls, Video, Audio, Language, amiibo, Saves (runtime/ui/menu.mm tabs_body with prelaunch set, in_game false). Prelaunch and amiibo have no rows that map to plain ini values (see skipped). The start screen's GAME FILES page (runtime/ui/launcher.mm, SETUP page) holds a few more settings: it is listed last as its own tab.
Platforms: 'windows' and 'linux' are the Vulkan builds; 'mac' is the Metal build (unmaintained). Rows without 'platforms' show everywhere.
Booleans are written as 0 / 1. Every key below is written by settings_save on every save, except hdr_paper_white (no row) and handheld_setup.
'enabledIf': the row is shown but greyed out (opt_disable_next) unless the condition holds. 'showIf': the row is only drawn when the condition holds.
'desc' strings that contain %d / %s / %.0f are formatted at run time; 'descExtra' paragraphs are appended only in the situation named.

rows.label: D-pad as left stick
rows.desc: The d-pad (and the arrow keys) also move like the left stick while the stick is at rest.
rows.note: Drawn as an Off / On combo with the description as a hint line under it (menu.mm toggle + hint), not an option row.

rows.label: PC mouse pointer
rows.desc: Point and click in menus and map. Esc pauses/goes back; F2 frees the cursor.

rows.label: Mouse camera
rows.desc: The mouse turns the camera. Pointer off: Esc frees it; pointer on: F2 frees it.
rows.note: Off / On combo with a hint line, not an option row.

rows.label: Mouse sensitivity
rows.desc: How fast the mouse turns the camera.
rows.note: Shown in percent; written as a fraction with two decimals (300% -> 3.00). Load accepts 0.1..10, else 3.00.

rows.label: Mouse vertical sensitivity
rows.desc: Up and down, as a percentage of the mouse sensitivity.
rows.note: Written with two decimals (100% -> 1.00). Load accepts 0.5..2, else 1.00.

rows.label: Invert mouse Y
rows.note: Off / On combo without a description.

rows.label: Mouse bow aiming
rows.desc: Hold the right mouse button to draw and aim your bow, click the left button to fire, and let go of the right button to put it away. While this is on, the right mouse button no longer raises the shield: bind the shield to another key under Key bindings.

rows.label: Controller rumble
rows.desc: Vibrate the controller during play.

rows.label: Rumble strength
rows.desc: 100% is the game's own.

rows.label: Free camera with both sticks
rows.desc: Clicking both sticks together turns the free camera on and off. Home on the keyboard always does. While it's on: F8 or d-pad up changes the filter, [ and ] or d-pad left and right the hour, F7 or d-pad down saves a picture in the screenshots folder.

rows.label: Controller camera speed
rows.desc: The right stick turns the camera faster than the game allows, at the two speeds below.

rows.label: Left and right speed
rows.desc: 100% is the game's own speed.

rows.label: Up and down speed
rows.desc: 100% is the game's own speed.

rows.label: Graphics preset
rows.desc: Sets the draw distance, shadows, upscaler, anti-aliasing, texture filtering and the Advanced options at once. Potato: for weak PCs (nearer, smaller shadows, FSR 1, no bloom or depth of field). Original: as on the console. High and Savage: further and sharper, for faster PCs.

multi.label: PC Handheld
multi.showIf: PC handheld only (settings_handheld: a Steam Deck or other PC handheld)

rows.note: The value shown is computed: the first preset whose draw_distance, shadow_resolution, bloom, depth_of_field, dynamic_resolution, anisotropy, antialias, game_fxaa, upscaler, async_shaders and render_scale all match (upscaler_quality only counts when upscaler is not off), else 'Custom' (shown, never picked). Applying a preset leaves upscaler_quality alone when the preset's upscaler is off. Does not wrap at the ends. Values above are Windows / Linux; on mac (UPSCALE_DEFAULT metalfx, TAA -> SMAA) Potato and Original/High/Savage write upscaler metalfx and Savage writes antialias smaa.

rows.label: Fullscreen
rows.desc: Fills the screen. Also: F11, Alt+Enter or Cmd+Ctrl+F.

rows.label: Fullscreen mode
rows.desc:
Automatic: borderless at your display's own size, the display switched to the size chosen at any other.

Borderless: never switches the display; another size is scaled to the screen. Quick to switch away from.

Exclusive: the display switched to the size chosen, at its highest refresh rate, its own size too.

rows.label: Monitor
rows.desc: The monitor the game is shown on, in a window or fullscreen. Automatic: where the window is (the primary monitor at start). A monitor that isn't connected is Automatic until it is.
rows.note: Then one choice per connected display n (1-based, SDL order, max 16): label '<n>: <name>  (<w> x <h>)' with ', primary' added inside the brackets for the primary display; ini value '<n> <name>' (e.g. 'display = 2 DELL U2720Q'). A saved display that is not connected is listed as '<name> (not connected)' and acts as Automatic.

rows.label: Window size
rows.desc:
The size of the game's window, or of the screen in fullscreen. Only the sizes your display can show: its own first, then grouped by shape. Any shape other than 16:9 is filled with Fill wide screens on; off, it keeps 16:9 with bars.

Your display: %d x %d.
rows.note: ini value '<w>x<h>' in pixels (load accepts 320x200 .. 16384x16384), or 'default' when never chosen (windowed: 1280x720, fullscreen: the desktop size; a PC handheld: its screen). Offered: of 640x360, 960x540, 1280x720, 1600x900, 1920x1080, 2560x1440, 3840x2160, 5120x2880, 7680x4320 (16:9); 1280x540, 1708x720, 1920x810, 2134x900, 2560x1080, 3440x1440, 3840x1600 (21:9); 1280x800, 1680x1050, 1920x1200, 2560x1600 (16:10); 640x480, 800x600, 1024x768, 1280x1024, 1600x1200 (4:3, 5:4) those that fit the display's desktop size (fullscreen: also bigger ones the display has a mode for), plus the desktop size itself, listed first; then grouped 16:9, 21:9, 16:10, 4:3+5:4, other, smallest first. Label '<w> x <h>  (<shape>)', the desktop size '(<shape>, native)'. Opened as a list (opt_list).

rows.label: Fill wide screens
rows.desc: On a window or screen that isn't 16:9 the game shows more of the world instead of black bars: to the sides when it's wider (21:9, 32:9), above and below when it's taller (16:10, 4:3). The HUD stays 16:9 in the middle; the pause menu, the map and the start screen are shown 16:9.

rows.label: HUD at edges
rows.desc: On windows taller than 16:9 with Fill wide screens, anchors the top and bottom HUD to the window edges.

rows.label: Field of view
rows.desc: How much of the world the camera shows in play: 100% is the game's own. Cutscenes and conversations keep theirs.

rows.label: HUD size
rows.desc: How big the hearts, stamina, minimap and the rest of the HUD are. Each part stays in its corner.

rows.label: Draw distance
rows.desc: How far out grass, trees, rocks, buildings and enemies appear. Higher costs more CPU and GPU time. Potato: nearer than on the console, for weak PCs.

rows.label: Frame rate
rows.desc: How many pictures a second the game draws. The game itself runs at the same speed at every rate (the console runs it at 30). Higher rates need a faster computer. Menus, cutscenes and conversations use it too, and videos play at their own speed. Off: as many as the computer can draw.
rows.descExtra: Your display refreshes %d times a second: a rate above that shows no more pictures, and one that divides it evenly is the smoothest.
rows.note: descExtra is added when the display's refresh rate is known. 'display' follows the display's own refresh rate (rounded, max 360). On a PC handheld the choices are 30, 40, 45, 60 FPS plus those of 90, 120, 144 up to the screen's refresh rate, with no Off and no Match display. A number that is not offered loads as the nearest offered rate.

rows.label: VSync
rows.desc: On: no tearing; the game waits for the display. With G-SYNC or FreeSync the display waits for the game instead: each frame shows as soon as it's ready, and the frame rate stays a little under the display's refresh rate. Fast: no tearing and no waiting: each refresh shows the newest frame. Adaptive: as On, but a frame that comes late shows at once and may tear. Off: each frame shows at once: the least delay, but it tears.
rows.descExtra: With On and Adaptive, the frame rate on this display goes up to about %d FPS.
rows.note: descExtra when the refresh rate is known (>= 30 Hz); %d = round(hz - hz*hz/3600).

rows.label: HDR
rows.desc: Automatic: while Windows HDR is on for this display, the picture is sent in HDR, so it looks as bright and colourful as in SDR (in SDR, Windows shows it dim and dull then). On: always in HDR, where the display takes it. Off: always SDR. White follows Windows' SDR content brightness (Settings > System > Display > HDR).

rows.label: Performance overlay
rows.desc: FPS: the frame rate and frame time. Full: also CPU, memory and GPU load and temperatures, a frame time graph and Link's coordinates. F10 switches between them while you play.

rows.label: Upscaler
rows.desc:
Off: the 3D image renders at the window's resolution. AMD FSR 1: it renders smaller (the mode below), then FSR 1's edge-aware upscaling and sharpening bring it to the window. The HUD and menus always render at the window's resolution.

AMD FSR 3: it renders smaller and builds the full-resolution image from the frames before, following the game's motion: sharper and steadier than FSR 1, and anti-aliased (Anti-aliasing has no effect with it). Sharpening sets its own sharpening. NVIDIA DLSS (NVIDIA RTX graphics cards) is coming in a later version.
rows.descAlt: Without FSR 3 on this PC the second paragraph is instead: "AMD FSR 3 and NVIDIA DLSS (NVIDIA RTX graphics cards) are coming in a later version."
rows.descExtra: AMD FSR 4: like FSR 3, but AMD's machine learning rebuilds the image. For AMD Radeon graphics cards on Windows. Sharpening sets its own sharpening.
rows.note: opt_choice_avail: an unavailable choice is shown greyed with its unavailableLabel and never stored. FSR 3 needs FSR 3 built in; FSR 4 needs an AMD Radeon with AMD's DLLs on Windows (shown 'FSR 4 (coming soon)' when offered but held back); DLSS needs NGX (vk_dlss_available). descExtra is added only when FSR 4 is available. Load maps metalfx -> fsr1.

rows.label: Upscaler
rows.desc:
How the game's image (1920 x 1080) is scaled up to a bigger window. Off: plain (bilinear) scaling. MetalFX: Apple's upscaler, sharper.

Rendering below the window's size (the modes below) is coming in a later version.
rows.note: Load maps fsr1 / fsr3 / fsr4 -> metalfx on mac.

rows.label: Upscaler mode
rows.desc:
How much smaller the game renders before the upscaler brings it to the window, on each side: Ultra Quality 1.3x, Quality 1.5x, Balanced 1.7x, Performance 2x, Ultra Performance 3x. Smaller is faster and softer.

Rendering at %.0f x %.0f.
rows.note: Ultra Performance is greyed (not offered) with FSR 3 / FSR 4 / DLSS below a 2160-line window. On mac (no render-target scaling) every mode is shown '<mode> (coming soon)' and the last paragraph reads 'Coming in a later version.'

rows.label: Anti-aliasing
rows.desc: FXAA: the game's own, as on the console: cheap, a little soft. Smooths jagged edges of the game image before it is scaled to the window. SMAA: finds the edges and blends only along them, so textures stay sharp. Most useful with an upscaler. TAA: blends each frame with the ones before it, following the game's motion, so edges stay smooth and stop shimmering; slightly softer, use it with Sharpening.
rows.note: Shown value (settings_aa_row): antialias=taa -> TAA, antialias=smaa -> SMAA, else game_fxaa=1 -> FXAA, else Off. Load also accepts antialias=fxaa (read as smaa) and forces game_fxaa=0 whenever antialias is not off.

rows.label: Anti-aliasing
rows.desc: Smooths jagged edges of the game image before it is scaled to the window. SMAA: finds the edges and blends only along them, so textures stay sharp. Most useful with an upscaler.
rows.note: Load reads taa as smaa on mac.

rows.label: Wet grass fix
rows.desc: In rain with the sun out, the game's wet lighting blows grass and roofs out to white. On: most of that glare goes, and the grass keeps its colour and a soft sheen. Applies from the next start.

rows.label: Render scale
rows.desc: Below 100% the game renders at a lower resolution than the window and is scaled up to it: faster, but blurrier (50% is a quarter of the pixels, for weak graphics cards). Above 100% it renders at a higher resolution and is scaled down to it, the cleanest way to smooth edges and shimmer. 200% is 4x the pixels: for fast graphics cards.

rows.label: Anisotropic filtering
rows.desc: Keeps the textures of ground, paths and walls sharp where you look along them into the distance. Off: the game's own filtering, as on the console. 16x is the sharpest and costs very little on a PC graphics card.

rows.label: Texture sharpness
rows.desc: Pulls forward mipmap levels on 3D textures for increased clarity on surfaces and distant objects. Sharp uses a -0.5 bias; Sharper uses -1.0.

rows.label: Sharpening (AMD CAS)
rows.desc: AMD FidelityFX CAS sharpens the 3D image after the upscaler (or at the window's resolution with the upscaler off), before the HUD is drawn over it: edges get crisper without halos. Most useful with AMD FSR 1.
rows.note: Stored internally as 0..10 and written *10 (percent); load rounds to the nearest 10.

rows.label: Frame generation (AMD FSR 3)
rows.desc: AMD FSR 3 makes a frame between each two the game draws: about twice the frames on screen. The frame rate above counts them all, so the game itself draws half of it (60 with 120) and the controls answer as at that rate, a little later. In play only: the menus and the map show the game's own frames. Fast moves can leave faint smears around Link and what moves on its own.

rows.label: Asynchronous shaders
rows.desc: On (default): the game never waits for a new shader to compile: what needs one still compiling is left out until it is ready, usually one frame (an effect pops in a frame late). Pictures the game draws only once (the save file's screenshot, the pause menu's background, terrain tiles) still wait for theirs. Off: every draw waits for its shader, a short stutter the first time an effect appears.

rows.label: Shadow resolution
rows.desc: The size of the maps the sun's shadows are drawn from. Console: the game's own, 896 x 896. High (2048), Ultra (4096) and Savage (8192) give sharper shadow edges (Link, trees, buildings) for more GPU time and video memory (Ultra: about 100 MB, Savage: about 400 MB). Savage is very heavy where there is a lot of foliage: in a forest it can cut the frame rate to a third, even on a fast GPU. Ultra or lower suits most GPUs. Potato (448): softer edges, for weak GPUs.

rows.label: Sharper text
rows.desc: Makes the game's letters sharper on 1440p and 4K screens. It takes effect the next time you start the game. This is an upscale made on your computer from the game's own letters, not Nintendo's original art: the shapes are kept, but they aren't exactly as drawn. 4x takes a moment longer to start and uses more video memory.

rows.label: Sharper menus
rows.desc: Makes the shapes and frames of the game's menus (panels, borders, icons drawn in one colour) sharper on 1440p and 4K screens. It takes effect the next time you start the game. This is an upscale made on your computer from the game's own art, not Nintendo's original art.

rows.label: Bloom
rows.desc: The glow around bright light: the sun, fire, glowing eyes. Off: a little faster, a flatter image.

rows.label: Depth of field
rows.desc: The game blurs the far distance a little. Off: sharp out to the horizon, a little faster.

rows.label: Dynamic resolution
rows.desc: As on the console: the game lowers its 3D resolution (down to 1280x720 before upscaling) while frames take long, and raises it again after. Off: always the full resolution. On with the Potato preset.

rows.label: Fast math
rows.desc: Your CPU has no FMA instructions, so the game's math runs in software. On: about 10% faster; some results round a tiny bit differently from the console, which doesn't show in play. Off: exact, as on the console.
rows.showIf: compatible game code only (gamelib_compat: a CPU without AVX2 / FMA)

rows.label: Haze
rows.desc: How hazy the air is. Lower: clearer distances. It takes effect the next time you start the game.

rows.label: Colour preset
rows.desc: Ready-made looks for the 3D image, made from the sliders below: Natural is the game's own colours, Warm and Cool shift the light, Vivid and Cinematic add contrast, Muted calms the colours. The HUD and menus keep their colours.
rows.note: Shown value: the preset whose five values all match, else 'Custom' (shown greyed, never picked). The LUT is not changed by a preset. colour_exposure is in EV with one decimal (stored as tenths).

rows.label: Exposure
rows.desc: Makes the 3D image brighter or darker, in stops: +1 EV is twice as bright.
rows.note: Written with one decimal ('%.1f').

rows.label: Contrast
rows.desc: More (or less) difference between dark and bright areas. Shadows and highlights keep their detail.

rows.label: Saturation
rows.desc: How strong the colours are. -100: black and white.

rows.label: Temperature
rows.desc: The colour of the light: below 0 cooler (bluer), above 0 warmer (more orange).

rows.label: Tint
rows.desc: Below 0 toward green, above 0 toward magenta: evens out a colour cast.

rows.label: LUT
rows.desc:
A look-up table (LUT) that recolours the 3D image. Savage Wind's own are listed first. Your own LUTs go in this folder: .cube files (up to 64 x 64 x 64) and ReShade-style .png strips (1024 x 32, 4096 x 64). They are listed by file name.

%s
rows.note: %s = the player's LUT folder (<data folder>/luts). The shipped LUTs (colour-luts/, sorted by name with Savage_Wind.cube moved first) are followed by the player's own .cube / .png files in <data folder>/luts, sorted by name: label = file name without extension, '_' shown as spaces; ini value = the file name itself (no prefix). The first setup sets sw:Savage_Wind.cube at 50% when no colour_lut is in the ini (see Game Files > Savage Wind colour look).

rows.label: LUT intensity
rows.desc: How much of the LUT's look is used: 100% is all of it, 0% none.

rows.label: Volume
rows.desc: The game's volume. 100% is the game's own level; above it, louder.
rows.note: Written with two decimals (100% -> 1.00); load clamps to 0..2.

rows.label: Shrine sensor volume
rows.desc: Volume of the Sheikah Slate sensor beeps. 0% silences the sensor.

rows.label: Audio output
rows.desc: Stereo: two-channel mix. Surround 5.1: all six channels (front, centre, subwoofer and rear) for a 5.1 speaker setup. 3D Headphones: binaural spatial mix of the six channels for headphones. Surround 5.1 is untested on real 5.1 speakers.

rows.label: Room reverb
rows.desc: The game's echo in caves, dungeons and big rooms.

rows.label: Movie audio
rows.desc: Sound in the game's movies (the opening and the ending). Applies the next time a movie starts.

rows.label: Mute in background
rows.desc: Mute audio while the game window is in the background or minimized.

rows.label: Text
rows.desc: The language of the game's texts and of these menus. Auto: your system's language (English if the game doesn't have it).
rows.note: Language names are shown as written (not translated). In game the description gets a restart paragraph; not in Configuration.

rows.label: Voices
rows.desc: The language the characters speak. Same as text: the voices the game picks for the text language (Japanese for Korean and Chinese, English for the other languages it has no voices for). Any other: those voices with any text language.

rows.label: Back up at each start
rows.desc: A copy of the save folder each time the game starts, if anything in it changed. The last 5 are kept in save-backups; the ones you make yourself are never removed.
rows.note: Greyed while an import / export / backup is running. The rest of the Saves tab (Profiles, Import, Export, Back up saves, Open save folder, Slots) is save management: skipped.

tabs.title: Game Files
tabs.page: The start screen's GAME FILES page (not a Settings tab). Rows below sit after 'Game files folder' and 'Folder path' in the section 'Set up again' once the game files are set up; before that (first start: 'Welcome to Savage Wind') they are in the section 'Set up'. All are greyed while a setup is running.

rows.label: Background
rows.desc: The picture behind this screen and while the game loads. A splash.jpg or splash.png of yours in the data folder always comes first.

rows.label: Loading picture
rows.desc: Shows that picture while the game loads. Turned off, the window stays black until the game's title screen: loading takes just as long.

rows.label: Precompile all shaders
rows.desc: After the setup, translates and compiles every shader of the game, so that none stutters the first time it is drawn, also in places never visited. A few more minutes and about 1.5 GB of disk. It can be done later too, from the game files page of Savage Wind Configuration.

rows.label: Savage Wind colour look
rows.desc: Recommended. The game's picture with Savage Wind's own colour look. Change it or turn it off any time in the game's Options > Colour (LUT).

multi.label: Off
multi.alsoIf: if the colour sliders match the Vivid preset (colour_exposure 0.0, colour_contrast 15, colour_saturation 30, colour_temperature 0, colour_tint 0), also set Natural: colour_contrast 0, colour_saturation 0 (exposure, temperature, tint 0)

multi.label: On
multi.alsoIf: if the colour sliders match Natural (all five 0), also set Vivid: colour_exposure 0.0, colour_contrast 15, colour_saturation 30, colour_temperature 0, colour_tint 0

rows.note: Shown On exactly when colour_lut = sw:Savage_Wind.cube. Before the first setup, if the ini has no colour_lut key at all, the page itself sets the On values (and Vivid over Natural).

rows.label: Slate Companion
rows.desc: Lets Slate Companion, a companion app for Breath of the Wild with a live map, guides and checklists, show where Link is while you play. It can only read the game, never change it, and only apps on this computer can connect. Turning it off takes effect the next time Savage Wind starts.

rows.label: Check for updates
rows.desc: When Savage Wind Configuration opens, asks GitHub if there is a new version and offers it. Nothing is installed until you press Update.
rows.showIf: a shipped release (post_update_shipped: Windows with sw-manifest.txt, Linux AppImage)

rows.label: Open this screen first
rows.desc: Starting Savage Wind opens this screen, where updates are offered. Turned off, savagewind.exe goes straight into the game.
rows.showIf: a shipped release (post_update_shipped: Windows with sw-manifest.txt, Linux AppImage)

Buttons Show in Explorer / Open folder / Show in Finder, Delete game files (with Delete / Cancel popup), Make a problem report, Import fonts, Use substitute font, and the Launch options section (launch_flags_ui: launch options, skipped by request).

skipped.why: Key binding remaps (bind_pad_* / bind_key_* keys), skipped by request.

Saves: Import from Wii U / Cemu..., Export to Wii U / Cemu..., Back up saves, Open save folder, Slots

Game Files: Go back to the previous version
